settings.label: Free game
settings.help: Battles for bragging rights: ships still sink and the overlay still runs, but no points are won or lost. Chat gets the Free game messages instead, so nothing mentions points.

settings.default: points
settings.label: Points variable
settings.help: The Streamer.bot user variable that holds each viewer's points. Currency Core by StreamUP and LOYALTY POINTS by tawmae are found on their own and win over this box; only change it for a points system of your own.

settings.default: Points
settings.label: Shown in chat as
settings.help: What {points} says in chat, like 'Coins' or 'Doubloons'. Only the wording changes; the points variable stays the same.

settings.label: Win bonus
settings.help: Paid on top when a player sinks the whole enemy fleet. 0 for none: a win already pays every ship it sank. The chat's battle is played for fun and pays nothing.

settings.label: Minimum balance
settings.help: What a player needs to start a battle. 0 asks for the value of their own fleet, so nobody plays a battle they couldn't pay for losing.

settings.label: Daily winnings cap
settings.help: The most a player can win per day. 0 for no cap. Once it is reached, further wins pay nothing until the next day.

settings.label: Charge for damaged ships when a player runs out of time
settings.help: Without this, walking away one hit before a Carrier sinks dodges its whole value. A Carrier hit 4 times out of 5 costs 4/5 of it. Never applies during normal play.

settings.label: Never let a balance go below zero
settings.help: A player who can't cover a loss is charged only what they have.
Nothing is staked up front: sinking one of the Admiral's ships pays its value at once, and losing one of your own costs its value. The ship values are on the Fleet page.

settings.default: captain
settings.label: Skill
settings.help: Ensign fires at random and never repeats a square, about 59 shots to clear a Quick board. Captain fires at random until it lands a hit, then works the squares around it and follows a line of hits to both ends, about 36 shots. Admiral hunts like the Captain, and between hits only checks squares spaced to the shortest ship still afloat, so nothing can hide between them, about 30 shots.

settings.label: Blunder chance
settings.help: How often the Admiral throws away its plan and fires blind, from 0 (never) to 100 (always). A handicap that works on any skill level without letting it cheat.

settings.label: Return fire delay
settings.help: Pause between a shot and the Admiral's reply, in milliseconds, so the overlay reads as an exchange rather than one flash. 0 to 5000.
The Admiral never sees your board. It only knows where it has fired, what it found there and which ship lengths are still afloat, the same things you know about its fleet.

settings.label: To open fire
settings.help: From starting a battle to the first shot. Nothing has sunk yet, so running out here costs nothing. At least 5.

settings.label: Per turn
settings.help: From the Admiral's reply to the next shot. Running out ends the battle and settles whatever has sunk. There is no command to leave a battle: this clock is the way out. At least 5.

settings.label: First warning
settings.help: Seconds left on the turn when chat is warned and the countdown ring turns amber. 0 turns it off.

settings.label: Final warning
settings.help: Seconds left on the turn when chat is warned again and the ring pulses red. 0 turns it off.

settings.label: The clock in short
settings.help: What the four values above add up to, as they stand.

settings.label: Blitz · 6×6 · 3 ships
settings.help: A 6×6 board with a Carrier of 4, a Cruiser of 3 and a Destroyer of 2. Fills in the board and the ships; nothing is saved until you save.

settings.label: Quick · 8×8 · 3 ships
settings.help: An 8×8 board with a Carrier of 5, a Cruiser of 3 and a Destroyer of 2: the default, about 36 shots per battle.

settings.label: Classic · 10×10 · 5 ships
settings.help: The classic 10×10 board with all five ships.
A preset fills in the board size and which ships sail, with their lengths. Change anything afterwards as you like.

settings.label: Grid size
settings.help: Squares per side, from 5 (A1 to E5) to 12 (A1 to L12). Bigger boards make longer battles.

settings.label: Ships may not touch each other
settings.help: Keeps a one-square gap around every ship, so two ships never read as one long one and hunting is fairer.

settings.label: Carrier
settings.help: Sail with a Carrier. Both fleets always have the same ships.

settings.label: Carrier length
settings.help: How many squares the Carrier takes up.

settings.label: Carrier value
settings.help: What sinking the Carrier pays, and what losing it costs.

settings.label: Battleship
settings.help: Sail with a Battleship.

settings.label: Battleship length
settings.help: How many squares the Battleship takes up.

settings.label: Battleship value
settings.help: What sinking the Battleship pays, and what losing it costs.

settings.label: Cruiser
settings.help: Sail with a Cruiser.

settings.label: Cruiser length
settings.help: How many squares the Cruiser takes up.

settings.label: Cruiser value
settings.help: What sinking the Cruiser pays, and what losing it costs.

settings.label: Submarine
settings.help: Sail with a Submarine.

settings.label: Submarine length
settings.help: How many squares the Submarine takes up.

settings.label: Submarine value
settings.help: What sinking the Submarine pays, and what losing it costs.

settings.label: Destroyer
settings.help: Sail with a Destroyer.

settings.label: Destroyer length
settings.help: How many squares the Destroyer takes up.

settings.label: Destroyer value
settings.help: What sinking the Destroyer pays, and what losing it costs.

settings.label: The fleet in short
settings.help: The board, the ships that sail and about how many shots a battle takes, as the values stand.
Both sides always sail the same fleet. A ship's value is what sinking it pays and what losing it costs, settled the moment it goes down.

settings.label: Solo: one viewer against the Admiral
settings.help: Started with !battleship. Each player has their own battle and settles every sinking as it happens.

settings.label: Chat vs the Admiral: the whole chat votes on every shot
settings.help: Started with !seeschlacht. Anybody can take part, by clicking on stream or with !fire. Played for fun: no points.

settings.label: Team duel: one chat team against another
settings.help: A viewer challenges another, both sides take on players, and the winning side shares everyone's entry.

The whole chat is one fleet, played for fun: nobody pays and nobody wins points. Each round every viewer has one vote, a click on enemy waters or !fire B7, and when the round ends the square with the most votes is fired at.

settings.default: Chat
settings.label: Team name
settings.help: What the chat's fleet is called on the overlay and in chat, as {team}.

settings.label: Seconds per round
settings.help: Make it longer than your stream delay, or viewers are still voting on a picture from before the last shot. At least 5.

Every viewer's click counts, logged in to Twitch or not - nothing needs linking. Somebody logged out can vote again by reloading the page, which does no harm in a battle played for fun. A chat battle starts only when no other battle is running, and if nobody votes for as long as the turn clock allows, the chat breaks it off.

A viewer challenges another by name, or anybody with no name, and captains Team A; whoever accepts captains Team B. Everyone else then picks a side, and every member pays the entry fee. The sides take turns, one voting round each, and the side that sinks the other's fleet shares the pot. Each winner gets their own entry back whole; only the winnings on top take the Addicted cut and the daily cap.

settings.label: Entry fee
settings.help: What every member pays to join a side. 0 for a duel played for the record alone. With Free game on, nobody pays.

settings.label: Seconds to accept
settings.help: A challenge nobody takes up in time is dropped and the entry refunded. At least 10.

settings.label: Seconds to sign up
settings.help: From the moment the challenge is accepted. At least 10.

settings.label: Seconds per round
settings.help: One round is one side's shot. Longer than your stream delay, as for the chat's battle. At least 5.

settings.label: Lead limit (0 = none)
settings.help: How many more players one side may have than the other. With 1, a side is never more than one player ahead. 0 lets anybody join either side.

settings.label: Turns a side may pass
settings.help: A side that lets this many turns in a row pass without a vote gives up, and the other side wins. If nobody fired at all, the duel is called off and every entry refunded. At least 1.

A duel can be challenged only while nothing else runs, and nothing else starts until its last shot. Anonymous Heat clicks never count in a duel, so members vote with !fire or link their clicks once with !fire link.

The stop command ends whatever is running, solo battles, the chat's battle or a duel, and pays nothing more out: no win bonus, no pot, no charge for damaged ships. A duel's entries are refunded. Who may use it is set on the command in Streamer.bot.

The overlay is battleship_overlay.html in the folder below. The game writes it there and keeps it up to date, saving your previous copy as a .bak. Its background is transparent, so it layers over any scene.

settings.default: Overlay
settings.label: Overlay folder
settings.help: Relative to the Battleship Game folder, or a full path on any drive. Empty uses 'Overlay'.
Creates the scene, and in it a browser source the size of your canvas pointed at the overlay file. OBS has to be connected in Streamer.bot under Stream Apps > OBS Studio.

settings.label: Connection #
settings.help: Which of Streamer.bot's OBS connections to use, if you have more than one. 0 is the first.

settings.default: Battleship
settings.label: Scene
settings.help: The scene the source is added to. It is created if it doesn't exist yet.

settings.default: Battleship Overlay
settings.label: Source
settings.help: The browser source created in that scene. Nothing is touched if OBS already has a source of this name.

settings.label: Set the overlay up in OBS
settings.help: Writes the overlay file if it is missing, then creates the scene and the browser source, the size of your canvas. Save first: the setup reads the saved folder and names.
settings.confirm: This creates the scene if it is missing and adds a browser source the size of your canvas pointing at the overlay file, over the OBS connection set above. Save your changes first if you edited the folder or the names. Go ahead?

settings.label: Scale
settings.help: Scales the whole overlay. 100 is full size.

settings.label: Text size
settings.help: Scales the text only, on top of the overall scale.

settings.label: Result shown
settings.help: How long a finished battle stays up before it fades out. At least 1.

settings.default: The Admiral
settings.label: Opponent name
settings.help: What the CPU is called on the overlay and in chat, as {admiral}.

settings.label: The player's fleet roster
settings.help: The ship list with damage pips under the player's own board.

settings.label: The opponent's fleet roster
settings.help: The same list under enemy waters. Its pips show which of their ships your hits landed on; switch it off to keep that hidden. Whichever roster is hidden, the two boards stay level.

settings.label: Coordinates
settings.help: The letters and numbers along the boards.

settings.label: Turn countdown ring
settings.help: Turns amber at the first warning and pulses red at the final one.

settings.label: Running score and accuracy
settings.help: Shots, hits and the battle's running total.

settings.label: Animations
settings.help: Impact bursts, the marker on the last shot and the pulsing final-warning ring.

settings.label: Hide the overlay during Free game
settings.help: Nothing is drawn while Free game is on.

settings.default: #ff5a3c
settings.label: Hit
settings.help: A square where a shot hit a ship.

settings.default: #8fb8d8
settings.label: Miss
settings.help: A square where a shot found only water.

settings.label: Sunk
settings.help: A ship that has gone down.

settings.default: #5b6b7c
settings.label: Ship hull
settings.help: Your own ships on the left-hand board.

settings.default: #4a7fa5
settings.label: Grid lines
settings.help: The lines between the squares.

settings.label: Water
settings.help: The squares nobody has fired at.

settings.label: Background
settings.help: The panel behind the boards, as solid as the opacity below makes it.

settings.label: Background opacity
settings.help: 0 keeps the overlay fully transparent, which is what most scenes want.
Your own fleet is drawn in full and the Admiral's waters stay fogged until something is hit. The Admiral reads neither chat nor the overlay, so showing your ships gives nothing away.

Heat is a free Twitch extension that passes viewers' clicks on your video to the overlay. With this on, the player whose battle is on screen can fire by clicking a square in enemy waters, and !fire keeps working as before.

settings.label: Fire by clicking the stream
settings.help: Twitch only: Heat is a Twitch extension. Needs Heat on your channel and Streamer.bot's WebSocket server running, see Setup below.

settings.label: First click takes control
settings.help: The first click in a player's battle takes control: Heat doesn't say who clicked, so the first viewer to click enemy waters in a player's battle is taken to be that player, for that battle. It holds back when another viewer clicked there in the last 20 seconds, or when the clicker is linked to a different player. A player whose battle was taken over clicks once and types !fire link, which also makes a link that lasts. Off, every player links with !fire link.

1. Install Heat on your channel and activate it as an Overlay extension: https://dashboard.twitch.tv/extensions/cr20njfkgll4okyrhag7xxph270sqk
2. Start Streamer.bot's WebSocket server: Servers/Clients > WebSocket Server, tick Auto Start, then Start Server. The overlay hands every click to the Battleship Game action through it.
3. Players just click. If someone else's click got in first, or the switch above is off, the player clicks once and types !fire link; that link is remembered for later battles.
Heat works in desktop browsers only: Twitch shows no overlay extensions in its mobile app, so phone viewers keep using !fire.

settings.label: Twitch channel ID
settings.help: The number Heat files your viewers' clicks under: your channel's user ID, not its name. Leave it empty to use the broadcaster account connected to Streamer.bot.

settings.label: Streamer.bot WebSocket
settings.help: Where the overlay reaches Streamer.bot: the address and port under Servers/Clients > WebSocket Server. Usually ws://127.0.0.1:8080/

settings.label: The broadcaster account
settings.help: The Twitch account connected to Streamer.bot, used whenever the channel ID box is empty.

settings.label: WebSocket password
settings.help: Only if you switched on authentication for the WebSocket server. It is stored in plain text next to the overlay, because the overlay has to read it.

Heat reports each click as a spot on the whole stream picture. That lines up by itself when the overlay's browser source covers the whole canvas, which is how OBS auto-setup creates it. If you moved or resized the source, say where it sits in percent of the canvas: a source shrunk to half size in the bottom-right corner is 50 / 50 / 50 / 50.

settings.label: Left
settings.help: How far from the left edge of the canvas the source starts.

settings.label: Top
settings.help: How far from the top of the canvas the source starts.

settings.label: Width
settings.help: How much of the canvas width the source covers. 100 is all of it.

settings.label: Height
settings.help: How much of the canvas height the source covers. 100 is all of it.

settings.label: Show every click on the overlay (alignment test)
settings.help: Draws a marker wherever anyone clicks, with the connection status in the top-left corner. Viewers see it too, so switch it off once the markers land where you click.

To check, switch the test on and save, then while you are live open your channel in a browser and click around the video. Each marker should land under the pointer. The player's own clicks show in gold, named after the square they fire at.

Optional. Heat's own Markers overlay pins a marker where each viewer last clicked, so everyone sees the clicks land. The button adds it to the scene named on the Overlay page, at the size of your canvas, over the same OBS connection.

settings.default: Heat Click Markers
settings.label: Markers source
settings.help: The browser source created for Heat's markers. Nothing is touched if OBS already has a source of this name.

settings.label: Add to OBS
settings.help: Adds a browser source showing https://heat.j38.net/markers/?channel=<your channel ID> to the overlay's scene. Save first: it reads the saved channel ID and names.
settings.confirm: This adds a browser source showing Heat's click markers for your channel to the overlay's scene (created if it is missing), at the size of your canvas, over the OBS connection on the Overlay page. Save first if you changed the channel ID or the names. Go ahead?

settings.help: What chat is told about linking is on the Messages page, under Click to Fire.

Twitch, YouTube and Kick all play, and every reply goes to the chat the command came from. To leave a platform out, untick it on the game's commands in Streamer.bot, for example 'Kick Message'. Click to Fire and the fleet whisper work on Twitch only.

settings.label: Whisper each player their fleet
settings.help: Twitch only: Streamer.bot can't whisper on YouTube or Kick. Twitch drops whispers from accounts without a verified phone number; a failure is logged and the battle goes on. The overlay already shows the player their fleet, so this is a private second copy.

settings.label: Everyone
settings.help: How long everyone waits after anybody starts a battle with !battleship, in seconds. 0 turns it off. Saving writes it onto the command in Streamer.bot.

settings.label: Per viewer
settings.help: How long one viewer waits before starting their next battle, in seconds. 0 turns it off. Saving writes it onto the command in Streamer.bot.

settings.label: Battles per hour (0 = none)
settings.help: How many battles one viewer may start per hour. 0 for no limit.
What chat is told while a cooldown runs is on the Messages page, under Cooldown.

settings.label: Blocked viewers
settings.help: Viewers who can't play at all, by their user name.

settings.default: ExampleGroup, TooAddictedToPlay, YourCustomBlockedGroup
settings.label: Blocked groups
settings.help: Streamer.bot user groups whose members can't play. Names must match the groups exactly.

settings.label: Addicted viewers
settings.help: Viewers who play as usual but win less: their winnings are cut by the Addicted cut below.

settings.label: Addicted groups
settings.help: Members of these Streamer.bot groups count as addicted too.

settings.label: Addicted cut
settings.help: How much of an addicted viewer's winnings is held back, from 0 (nothing) to 100 (all of it). 50 means they earn half. Losses are unaffected.

settings.default: net
settings.label: Rank players by
settings.help: What !ballstats ranks by. Net is the fair one, since losing ships costs points.

options.label: Net: everything won minus everything lost

settings.label: Places shown
settings.help: How many players !ballstats lists.

settings.label: Medals for the top three
settings.help: 🥇🥈🥉 in front of the first three places.
Every tracked value is kept in a persisted bsg_* user variable, so any other Streamer.bot action can read a player's record.

settings.label: Hide the broadcaster
settings.help: Matched by user ID, so a name change can't put them back on the board.

settings.label: Hide the bot account
settings.help: Matched by user ID.

settings.label: Bot account
settings.help: Send the leaderboard from your Streamer.bot bot account instead of the broadcaster account.

settings.label: Send as /me
settings.help: Twitch only: YouTube and Kick have no /me, so there the leaderboard always goes out as plain chat. On Twitch, sends it as a /me action.
The !bstats and !ballstats replies are on the Messages page, under Stats, and go out like the game's messages.

settings.default: off
settings.label: Automatic reset
settings.help: Clears the leaderboard on its own when the period rolls over, using the scope below. Switching it on never wipes anything at once: the current period is recorded first, and the reset happens at the next boundary.

settings.default: totals
settings.label: What a reset clears
settings.help: Totals only: points won, points lost and net. Battles, streaks and records are kept. Everything: every statistic of every player, a clean slate.

settings.label: Reset the leaderboard now
settings.help: Clears what 'What a reset clears' says, for every player, straight away. Save first: the reset reads the saved scope.
settings.confirm: This permanently clears the leaderboard for every player according to the reset scope above (saved). It cannot be undone. Continue?

settings.label: Write a log file per day
settings.help: Writes every finished battle - win, loss, timeout, the chat's battle and the duel - to a dated 'BSG-log-yyyy-MM-dd.txt' in the Logs folder, one file per day.

settings.default: 🛑 {user} has stopped {game}'s battle — nothing more is paid out.
settings.label: Battle stopped
settings.help: {user} is the moderator, {game} the player or the chat's team name. Nothing more is paid out.

settings.default: 🛑 {user} has stopped the duel — nothing is paid out, every entry is refunded.
settings.label: Duel stopped
settings.help: Every entry is refunded.

settings.default: @{user}, there is no battle or duel to stop.
settings.label: Nothing to stop
settings.help: The stop command with no battle or duel running.

settings.default: 🖱️ {user}, you can also fire by clicking enemy waters on stream — your first click there takes control. Did someone else's click get in first? Click once more, then type !fire link.
settings.label: How to fire by clicking
settings.help: Sent to a Twitch player without a link when their battle comes on screen, while the first click takes control. Leave it empty to send nothing.

settings.default: 🖱️ {user}, you can also fire by clicking enemy waters on stream: click any square, then type !fire link. Only once — after that your clicks fire on their own.
settings.label: How to link
settings.help: Sent at the same moment when the first click doesn't take control, so every player links with !fire link.

settings.default: 🖱️ {user}, your clicks are linked — from now on just click enemy waters on stream to fire.
settings.label: Linked
settings.help: Confirms !fire link. The click that made the link fires straight after.

settings.default: @{user}, no click on enemy waters reached me in the last {seconds} seconds. Click a square on stream first, then type !fire link.
settings.label: Link: no click seen
settings.help: !fire link found no click on enemy waters in the last seconds.

settings.default: @{user}, more than one person clicked enemy waters just now, so I can't tell which clicks are yours. Click again in a moment, then type !fire link.
settings.label: Link: more than one clicker
settings.help: Several viewers clicked in that time, so the link is refused rather than guessed.

settings.default: @{user}, '{input}' is not a square on this board. Use a letter and a number, like B7 (A1 to {max}).
settings.label: Not a square on the board
settings.help: !fire with something that isn't a square, like 'Z9'.

settings.default: @{user}, name a square to fire at, like !fire B7
settings.label: No square given
settings.help: !fire on its own.

settings.default: @{user}, you have already fired at {coord}. Pick another square — this one is free.
settings.label: Already fired there
settings.help: A repeat shot never costs the turn or the clock.

settings.default: @{user}, you have no battle running. Start one with !battleship
settings.label: No battle running
settings.help: !fire, !fleet or !board from a viewer with no battle.

settings.default: @{user}, you are already at sea. Fire with !fire B7.
settings.label: Already in a battle
settings.help: !battleship from a viewer whose battle is still running.

settings.default: @{user}, the battle has already started — you can only redeploy before your first shot.
settings.label: Too late to redeploy
settings.help: !fleet after the first shot.

settings.default: @{user}, you need at least {required} {points} to put a fleet to sea. You have {balance}.
settings.label: Not enough points
settings.help: Below the minimum balance on the Game page, or short of a duel's entry fee.

settings.default: @{user}, that game mode is switched off.
settings.label: Game mode switched off
settings.help: A mode switched off on the Modes page.

settings.default: @{user}, a battle is already running — {team} can take on {admiral} once it is over.
settings.label: Chat battle has to wait
settings.help: The chat's battle starts only when no other battle is running.

settings.default: @{user}, you have hit the limit of {max} battles per hour.
settings.label: Too many battles this hour
settings.help: The limit on the Access page.

settings.default: @{user}, you have reached today's winnings cap of {cap} {points}. Further wins pay nothing until tomorrow.
settings.label: Daily winnings cap reached
settings.help: The cap on the Game page.

settings.default: @{user}, a battle or a duel is already on — try again once it is over.
settings.label: Duel has to wait
settings.help: A duel is challenged only while nothing else runs, and nothing else starts while one does.

settings.default: @{user}, there is no challenge waiting for you.
settings.label: No challenge to accept
settings.help: Nothing is waiting, it is somebody else's challenge, it is the caller's own, or its time has run out.

settings.default: @{user}, no duel is taking players right now.
settings.label: Sign-up isn't open
settings.help: The join command while no duel takes players.

settings.default: @{user}, you are already in {team}.
settings.label: Already on a side
settings.help: The join command from somebody who already joined.

settings.default: @{user}, {team} already has {gap} more players than {other} — join {other} instead.
settings.label: Side too far ahead
settings.help: Only with a lead limit on the Modes page.

settings.default: @{user}, pick a side: !team A or !team B — or just !team to fill the smaller one.
settings.label: No such side
settings.help: The join command named neither A nor B nor anybody on a side.

settings.default: @{user}, only the two teams vote in this duel.
settings.label: Not in the duel
settings.help: A !fire vote from somebody on neither side.

settings.default: @{user}, it is {team}'s turn.
settings.label: Not this side's turn
settings.help: {team} is the side whose turn it is.

settings.default: Your fleet is deployed: {fleet}. The Admiral cannot read this — or your chat. Good hunting!
settings.label: Your fleet
settings.help: Whispered to a solo player when their battle starts, while the whisper is on.

settings.default: Battleship is on global cooldown. Try again in {seconds} seconds.
settings.label: Everyone
settings.help: Sent while the cooldown for everyone runs.

settings.default: @{user}, you're on cooldown. Try again in {seconds} seconds.
settings.label: Per viewer
settings.help: Sent while this viewer's own cooldown runs.

settings.default: @{user}: no battles fought yet. Start one with !battleship
settings.label: No record yet
settings.help: !bstats for a player with no battles.

settings.default: No battle records yet.
settings.label: Leaderboard empty
settings.help: !ballstats before anybody has a record.
